===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*seǵʰ-}}
[[Image:Moye Elementary School.JPG|thumb|Elementary school]]
From {{inh|en|enm|scole}}, from {{inh|en|ang|scōl|t=place of education}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*skōlu}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|schola}}, {{m|la|scola|t=learned discussion or dissertation, lecture, school}}, from {{der|en|grc|σχολή|t=spare time, leisure}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seǵʰ-|t=to hold, have, possess}}. {{doublet|en|schola|shul}}.

Compare {{cog|ofs|skūle}}, {{m|ofs|schūle|t=school}} ({{cog|fy|skoalle}}, {{cog|stq|Skoule}}), {{cog|nl|school|t=school}}, {{cog|nds-de|School|t=school}}, {{cog|goh|scuola|t=school}}, {{cog|de|Schule|t=school}}, {{cog|non|skóli|t=school}}.

Influenced in some senses by {{m+|enm|schole||group of persons, host, company}}, from {{cog|dum|scole||multitude, troop, band}}. See {{m|en|school||group|id=group}}. Related also to {{cog|goh|sigi|t=victory|tr={{cog|de|Sieg}}}}, {{cog|ang|siġe}}, {{m|ang|sigor|t=victory}}.

====Alternative forms====
* {{alter|en|schole||obsolete}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|India|North America}} An [[institution]] dedicated to [[teaching]] and [[learning]]; an [[educational]] institution.
#: {{syn|en|academy|college|university}}
#: {{ux|en|Our children attend a public '''school''' in our neighborhood.}}
#: {{ux|en|Harvard University is a famous American postsecondary '''school'''.}}
# {{lb|en|British}} An [[educational institution]] providing [[primary education|primary]] and [[secondary education]], prior to [[tertiary education]] ([[college]] or [[university]]).
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-19| author=[http://www.theguardian.com/profile/marktran Mark Tran]| volume=189| issue=6| page=1| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2013/jul/12/war-denying-children-education Denied an education by war]| passage=One particularly damaging, but often ignored, effect of conflict on education is the proliferation of attacks on '''schools'''{{...}}as children, teachers or '''school''' buildings become the targets of attacks. Parents fear sending their children to '''school'''. Girls are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.}}
# {{lb|en|UK}} At {{w|Eton College}}, a [[period]] or session of teaching.
#: {{ux|en|Divinity, history and geography are studied for two '''schools''' per week.}}
# Within a larger educational institution, an organizational unit, such as a [[department]] or [[institute]], which is dedicated to a specific subject area.
#: {{syn|en|college|department|faculty|institute}}
#: {{ux|en|We are enrolled in the same university, but I attend the '''School''' of Economics and my brother is in the '''School''' of Music.}}
# An [[art movement]], a community of artists.
#: {{ux|en|The Barbizon '''school''' of painters were part of an art movement towards Realism in art, which arose in the context of the dominant Romantic movement of the time.}}
# {{qualifier|considered collectively}} The followers of a particular doctrine; a particular way of thinking or particular doctrine; a [[school of thought]].
#: {{ux|en|These economists belong to the monetarist '''school'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Taylor Worthy Communicant|year=1661|pages=90–91|pageref=91|passage=Let no man be leſſe confident in his holy faith {{...}} by reason of any difference of judgement vvhich is in the ſeveral '''Schools''' of Chriſtians concerning the effects and conſequent bleſſings of this Sacrament.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=3|passage=Here the stripped panelling was warmly gold and the pictures, mostly of the English '''school''', were mellow and gentle in the afternoon light.}}
# The time during which classes are attended or in session in an educational institution.
#: {{ux|en|I’ll see you after '''school'''.}}
# <!--outdated?-->The room or hall in English universities where the examinations for degrees and honours are held.
# The canons, precepts, or body of opinion or practice, sanctioned by the authority of a particular class or age.
#: {{ux|en|He was a gentleman of the old '''school'''.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1883|author=w:Arthur Sherburne Hardy|title=But Yet a Woman|passage=His face pale but striking, though not handsome after the '''schools'''.}}
# An establishment offering specialized instruction, as for driving, cooking, typing, coding, etc.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[educate]], [[teach]], or [[train]] (often, but not necessarily, in a school).
#: {{ux|en|Many future prime ministers were '''schooled''' in Eton.}}
#* {{RQ:Dekker Dreame|page=35|passage=''I tooke delights'' / ''In plucking Apples from'' t’Heſperian Trees, / ''Which'' Eating, ''I grew'' Learn’d: ''adde to'' All theſe / ''My'' Priuate Readings, ''which more'' '''School’d''' ''my'' Soule, / ''Then'' Tutors, ''when they ſternliest did'' Controll / ''With'' Frownes ''or'' Rods'':'' {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[defeat]] [[emphatically]], to teach an [[opponent]] a [[harsh]] [[lesson]].
#* {{quote-journal |en |date=April 13, 1998 |author=Leigh Jones |title=National Bar Exam Methods Win in ADA Regulation Test |journal=w:The Journal Record |passage=A blind law graduate who put the National Conference of Bar Examiners to the test got '''schooled''' in federal court.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Steve Smith|title=Forever Red: Confessions of a Cornhusker Football Fan|page=67
|passage=Two weeks later, the Cornhuskers put on their road whites again and promptly got '''schooled''' by miserable Iowa State in Ames. After the shocking loss {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Peter David; Alvin Sargent|title=Spider-Man 3|pageurl=http://books.google.com/books?id=lQi3QO6h9UoC&pg=PA216&dq=%22gonna+school+you%22&lr=&sig=dpEAXzEMHzrxZQAgCEA0GaPEQDY|page=216|publisher=Simon and Schuster|isbn=1416527214

===Etymology 2===
{{etymid|en|group}}
From {{inh|en|enm|scole}}, {{m|enm|schole||group of persons, multitude, host, school of fish}}, from {{der|en|dum|scole||multitude, troop of people, swarm of animals}}, from {{der|en|odt|*scola}}, {{m|odt|*skola||troop, multitude}}, from {{der|en|frk|*skolu}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skulō||crowd}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kʷel-||crowd, people}}.

Cognate with {{cog|gml|schōle||multitude, troop}}, {{cog|ang|scolu||troop or band of people, host, multitude, school of fish}}. {{doublet|en|shoal|id1=fish}}.

====Noun====
[[File:Sixfinger threadfin school.jpg|thumb|A school ({{senseno|en|group-of-fish}}) of [[fish]]]]
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|group-of-fish}} {{cln|en|collective nouns}} {{lb|en|collective}} A group of [[fish]] or a group of [[marine]] [[mammals]] such as [[porpoise]]s, [[dolphin]]s, or [[whale]]s.
#: {{syn|en|shoal}}
#: {{ux|en|The divers encountered a huge '''school''' of mackerel.}}
# A [[multitude]].
